Several levels may therefore be similar, either to cover different curriculum standards or to support gradual progression.
As an example, suppose the task is to sort even and odd numbers.
The numbers in that example would range from 10 to 180.
Dividing that range into 6 similar levels might work better.
The first level could cover numbers from 10 to 40.
A second level could then cover the range from 40 to 90.
The third level could cover numbers from 90 through 180.
The reason for splitting the skill is that teachers address these numbers in 7 different blocks.
